newsitem.title: INDIA: India's DMK says RJD issue not resolved yet.
newsitem.headline: India's DMK says RJD issue not resolved yet.

text.p: India's Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party said on Friday that the United Front had not yet resolved its problem on the admittance of the breakaway Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) group of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal.
DMK president Muthuvel Karunanidhi told reporters in Madras that the alliance's Steering Committee will discuss the issue on July 25, when he expected the problem to be resolved.

Information and Broadcasting Minister Jaipal Reddy said after a meeting of senior alliance leaders on Thursday that the United Front had decided not to admit the RJD, whose leader Laloo Prasad Yadav has been indicted in a corruption scandal.
Yadav says he is innocent in the $280 million scandal, but has faced pressure from communists in the coalition to resign as chief minister of his state, Bihar.

"No decision on RJD's admission was taken at yesterday's meeting. Only by rushing to the press with such hasty statements, unnecessary confusion is being caused," Karunanidhi, who is also Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu state, said.
The DMK president said he had argued for RJD's presence in the coalition during Thursday's meeting and had received support from other alliance leaders.

"It was only decided that all issues would be sorted out on July 25 when the United Front Steering Committee will meet after swearing in of the President," he said. "I hope that a satisfactory solution would be found."

The DMK threatened to pull out of Gujral's government on Monday, citing differences with coalition partners on how to deal with the RJD, which was formed on July 5 following differences in the Janata Dal over leadership elections.
"My statement on Monday was aimed at averting a mid-term election," Karunanidhi said.
